title: They get diluted
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Have you ever bought something big with money you did not have yet?

groups.heading: He's getting deeper and deeper, and leveraging

lines.text: Jose said he would prepare the class to read the chapter, because it is very dense, with a lot of business decisions the author is making.
As Jose retells it, the author wants to diversify. He realizes the billboard business is under threat. He wants a television station.
Now it is not just putting an ad on a billboard, Jose said. There are all these moving parts: the antenna, the content, selling the advertising. You can see the complexity.
He is burning money, Jose said. Some of the radio stations are losing money. He is getting deeper and deeper, and leveraging.
Leveraging, Jose said, is when you use an asset to acquire another asset, using debt or equity. Normally that is what they call it.

groups.heading: They get diluted, like adding water to orange juice

lines.text: Jose gave a short lesson on shares. Imagine two founders who split a company, fifty each. An investor asks what it is worth. A million dollars. The investor wants ten percent, for a hundred thousand.
Then there is a word, dilution. They get diluted, like adding water to orange juice. You don't have as much stock of the company anymore, because you sold stock to take cash in.

A student asked: I thought diluting meant printing more shares. Jose said: not necessarily. Even if you print more shares, it is all based on the valuation. You go down in your value because you are selling part of the company.
As Jose retells the chapter, the author's ownership dropped below half, but he kept the voting stock.
So be very careful as entrepreneurs, Jose said. Are you selling the company too quickly, before you build value in it? And are you losing control of the voting shares?
What would you be willing to sell, and what would you never give up?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you own or control now: a skill, money, a project, a client list.
Write what you would borrow or sell to grow it.
If you sold ten percent of your project, what would you give up?
Write who you would let hold a vote, and who you would not.
Write the one thing you would never give up.

choices: Using an asset to acquire another asset, using debt or equity

check.q: What did Jose say diluting is like?
Which two cautions did Jose give entrepreneurs?
choices: Selling too quickly before building value, and losing control of the voting shares
Spending too much on ads, and hiring too slowly
Starting too early, and working too hard

recap: Know what you give up when you borrow or sell. Don't sell too soon, and keep control.
